summary: Shenghai Li specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (2004–2012) under Donald R. Davis Jr., later holding posts at Harvard University (2013–2015) and the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (2015–2016).

Shenpen Hookham works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Reading (~1965–1968) and earned a D.Phil from the University of Oxford (~1980–1986) under Michael M. Broido, alongside training under several traditional teachers.

Shenphen Nangwa worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under teachers including Patrul Rinpoche and Önpo Tenzin Norbu, taught at Dzogchen Monastery in 1902, and founded Dzongsar Monastery, serving as its first shedra khenpo in 1918.

Sherab Chomphel specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the College for Higher Tibetan Studies (B.A., 2012–2015), Banaras Hindu University (M.A., 2016–2018), and Harvard University (MTS, 2022–2025).

Sherab Gyatso worked in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, earning a Geshe degree at Drepung Monastery (1896–1916). He founded the Buddhist Association of China in 1952, serving as its president (~1953–1966), and became dean of the Buddhist Academy of China (1956).

Sherry B. Ortner is an anthropologist in Tibetology and religious studies who studied at Bryn Mawr College and the University of Chicago. She held academic posts at Sarah Lawrence College (~1971–1977), the University of Michigan (~1977–1994), and UCLA (~2004).
Sherry Chayat is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Vassar College (~1961–1965) and trained under traditional teacher Eido Shimano (~1967–1977).
Shesh Dev Pandey is an Indologist who completed a Shastri degree at Banaras Hindu University between 2020 and 2023, where he held the post of student in 2020.

Shi Hu worked in philosophy, sinology, and history and archaeology. After earning a PhD at Columbia University under John Dewey (~1915–1917), he held posts at Peking University (~1917–1937) and Academia Sinica (1958–1962).

Shi Wang works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Wang earned a BA at Yale University (2020–2024) and undertook DPhil studies at the University of Oxford (2024–2025).

Shichang Ma worked in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He was a researcher in Buddhist archaeology at the Dunhuang Academy (1963–1978) and joined the Archaeology Department at Peking University in 1982.
Shigeki Kaizuka was a scholar of sinology and history and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University from ~1925 to 1928 and later held a post there from ~1949 to 1968.
Shigeki Kudo is a Buddhist studies scholar who held assistant and associate professor posts at Kyoto University, Shuchiin University, and Shitennoji University (attested 1972–1973).

Shigeki Moro works in Buddhist studies, computational fields, and philosophy. Educated at Waseda, Toyo, and Kansai universities, he served as professor at Hanazono University (2002–2025) and became professor at Waseda University in 2025.
Shigemasa Fukui specializes in sinology and history and archaeology. He completed his studies at Waseda University (~1954–1963) and later served as a professor there from ~1980 to 2006.

Shigemitsu Dando studied under Seiichiro Ono at the University of Tokyo (~1932–1935). He later held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1937–1974), Keio University, and the Supreme Court of Japan (~1974–1983).
Shigenori Nagatomo works in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, serving as a professor of religious studies at Temple University (attested in 1999 and 2017).

Shigeo Kamata specialized in Buddhist studies and sinology, completing doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1960–1988), Aichi Gakuin University (~1988–1996), and Matsugaoka Bunko (~1988–2001).
Shigeo Yokoyama studied at Kyoto University (~1974–1982) and works in religious studies. He held academic posts at Okayama University (~1987–1996) and Nara Women's University (~1996–2019).

Shigeru Gorai studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University. He worked in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology, holding posts at Otani University (1955–1978), Koyasan University (~1963–1973), and the Institute of Japanese Religious Folklore (~1974–1993).
